title: Blinking Through the Readings

patient.name: Mdm Phua Siew Eng
patient.presenting_complaint: Here for auto-refraction and keratometry; the readings keep coming out inconsistent

history.hpc: Mdm Phua attends for auto-refraction and keratometry as a new patient work-up. The machine keeps producing scattered, inconsistent values. She says: 'My eyes very dry, the machine ask me to look but I keep wanting to blink.' She has dry eye symptoms, worse with air-conditioning and screen work. The OT must recognise the unreliable readings and improve the tear film and technique.
history.social_hx: Office worker, long screen hours in an air-conditioned office. Non-smoker.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Dry ocular surface; otherwise normal. An unstable tear film degrades auto-refraction/keratometry readings.

investigations.auto_refraction_keratometry: Initial AR/AK readings inconsistent (scattered sphere/cylinder and K values) due to an unstable tear film. The OT asked the patient to blink fully to refresh the tear film (and instilled a lubricant), optimised positioning and fixation, and re-acquired. Repeat readings became consistent and were documented as a useful starting point for refraction.
investigations.measurement_quality: First attempt scattered/unreliable; after blinking/lubrication and re-positioning, readings consistent across repeats.

diagnosis: Unreliable auto-refraction/keratometry caused by an unstable tear film (dry eye), corrected by refreshing the tear film and optimising technique to obtain consistent readings. The OT competency is recognising unreliable readings, improving the surface/technique, and documenting; the final prescription is set by the doctor/optometrist on subjective refraction.

immediate: Recognise scattered, inconsistent AR/AK values as unreliable rather than a true measurement
Ask the patient to blink fully to refresh the tear film and instil a lubricant drop if needed
Optimise positioning, fixation, and alignment before re-acquiring
Take multiple readings and confirm consistency before accepting
Document the AR/AK values as an objective starting point and note the tear-film issue
Avoid using a single unstable reading; present consistent values for the doctor/optometrist
follow_up: Doctor/optometrist to perform subjective refraction to confirm the prescription
Consider managing the dry eye to improve future measurements and comfort
Keep the AR/AK as a starting reference for refraction
patient_education: Explain that dry eyes can make the machine readings jump around, so blinking helps
Explain the lubricant drop and full blinks improve accuracy
Explain the readings are a starting point and the doctor/optometrist fine-tunes the glasses
Offer simple dry-eye advice (regular blinking breaks from screens, lubricants)
